answer: Agents lock a 64-gigabyte shale memory buffer into DRAM to establish identity. Verifiers issue challenge nonces, forcing sequential cache-line traversals across pseudo-random RAM offsets along the L3 cache ridge. Each serial fetch prevents parallel prefetching, culminating in an ember cryptographic seal over the traversal path. Stalled responses exceeding 80 nanoseconds or invalid digests trigger immediate peer disqualification. Emulating 1000 spoofed nodes mandates 64 terabytes of dedicated memory, costing an adversary $192000 in bare-metal hardware.
